thread.title: Can Apple Services Growth Offset Slowing iPhone Business?

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Can Apple Services Growth Offset Slowing iPhone Business?
text:
While Apple ( AAPL ) investors have fixated on slowing iPhone sales and the maturing smartphone business, they are underappreciating the company's fast-growing services segment, according to a Wall Street analyst.
X "We think investors have been hyperfocused on the iPhone unit trends and less focused on Apple's ability to grow and monetize the installed base," RBC Capital Markets analyst Amit Daryanani says in a report to clients. Apple's services segment is a key growth area for investors to consider because the company has an installed base of 1.3 billion iOS devices, he said.
Apple's services have the "ability to lift gross (profit) margins, reduce cyclicality, and improve valuation," Daryanani said. "Fundamentally, Apple's Services business is a critical part of the investment thesis, particularly as the smartphone market matures."
Apple has a goal to grow its services business to about $48 billion to $50 billion in annual sales by 2020. It is now generating more than $31 billion a year in services revenue, or about 13% of Apple's total sales, Daryanani said in the report, released late Monday.

Please contact customer service CLOSE RBC estimates that Apple gets about 36% of its services revenue from the App Store, 17% from iTunes and 17% from AppleCare. Apple Music accounts for about 9% and iCloud for 5%, it said. The rest is made up of Apple Pay, licensing fees and miscellaneous services.
RBC estimates that Apple's services segment generates a gross profit margin of about 60%, compared with about 38% for the total company.
Daryanani reiterated his outperform rating on Apple stock with a price target of 205.
Apple shares slipped 6 cents to close at 175.24 on the stock market today . Apple hit a record high of 183.50 on March 13.
"We believe Apple stock should continue to outperform the market driven by strong free-cash-flow generation, ability for outsized capital allocation and a growing iOS install base that generates sustained and recurring free-cash-flow growth," he said.
